0.48.0.notes:
feat: hide customers' personal details from staff who have not been given permission to see them, stop customer information being left behind on shared computers, and let admins mark extra personal questions on a customer's form the same way
- A customer's personal details - ID card number, phone numbers, email address, date of birth, photo and exact street address - are now hidden from staff unless they have been given permission to see them. In place of the real value staff see a partly hidden one: a phone number shows only its last four digits, an email address shows only its first letter and the part after the @, and a date of birth shows only the year.
- Enough is left showing to still do the job. An agent who has been given a phone number over the line can still tell which customer it belongs to from the last four digits, and searching for a customer by their full phone number still finds them.
- The broader parts of an address - country, province, district, sub-district and postcode - stay visible to everyone. The area and zone screens rely on them, and on their own they do not point to a particular household.
- A customer's photo is replaced with the same blank picture already used for customers who have no photo on file.
- Where a customer is opened for editing, the protected fields are shown locked and empty rather than partly hidden. This is deliberate: a partly hidden value sitting in an editable box would be saved over the real one the moment somebody pressed save. Everything else on the form - notes, customer type and so on - can still be changed and saved as normal, and the hidden details are left exactly as they were.
- Adding a brand new customer is unaffected. Every field can be filled in as before, since there is nothing on file yet to hide.
- Extra phone numbers and email addresses kept alongside the main ones are hidden the same way. LINE, Facebook and Text Chat account names stay visible, as those are account names rather than ways of contacting somebody directly.
- Staff without permission can no longer open an extra phone number or email address for editing, although they can still remove one.
- Who may see all of this is controlled by a single new permission, granted by the system administrator in the usual way. Nobody holds it until it is granted, so details start out hidden rather than exposed. System administrators can always see them.
- The number shown for a case itself - the phone number the caller actually used to open it - is not affected by any of this and is always shown in full. It is kept separately from the customer's own phone number on file, since a customer can call in on a number that is not their own.
- When building a customer's "specific form" (the extra custom questions some customer types have), whoever designs the form can now tick a new "Contains personal data" box on a question and choose how it should be hidden - showing only the last four digits, only the year, in an email-style partial hide, or fully hidden - and it is then treated exactly like the built-in personal details above: hidden on the customer's page and locked (not saveable-over) when editing. This does not apply to the questions on case forms or other question sets elsewhere in the app - only to a customer's own specific form.
- Signing out now clears the case information the app keeps on the computer for working offline. Until now it stayed on the machine after signing out, so on a shared workstation the next person to sign in inherited the previous person's cases. A problem clearing it cannot stop somebody signing out.
- Case information is no longer passed around inside the app in a way that left the whole case list - including customer names, phone numbers and addresses - readable by anything else running on the page. Screens are now simply told that something has changed and look the case up themselves, which is what most of them already did.
- The case board still keeps itself up to date exactly as before, including when a case is created or changed by another dispatcher.
- Web addresses and error messages written to the browser's technical log no longer carry customer details. Looking a customer up by ID card number or phone number previously wrote that number into the log.
- Available in Thai and English. The new "Contains personal data" question-builder wording is not yet available in Chinese, matching the rest of the form-builder screen, which has never had a Chinese translation.

feat(cms): show the driving route, distance and estimated arrival time from a selected officer to the case
- Opening a staff member's card on the case map now offers a "Calculate route" button. Pressing it draws the driving route from that officer's last known position to the case on the map, and shows the distance and how long the drive should take.
- A separate summary shows the estimated time of arrival as a clock time, and how much time is left before they arrive, so nobody has to work it out from the drive time alone.

- If the officer's position is more than a few minutes old, the calculated route is still shown but is clearly marked as based on an outdated position.

0.32.1.notes:
fix(core): migrate UserProfile off raw fetch onto RTK Query + GraphQL, and authenticate the password-reset endpoint
- user.ts (types): add ChangePasswordData ({id, currentPassword, newPassword}) and ResetPasswordData ({email, username, newPassword}); neither existed anywhere in the repo - authApi.ts's commented-out ChangePasswordData/ResetPasswordData imports reference types that were never defined
- userApi.ts: add changePassword (PATCH /users/change_password/:id, id carried in the path) and resetPassword (POST /users/reset_password) mutations plus their hooks, contracts per src/core/mocks/userCURL.v2.sh:325-355; placed in userApi rather than authApi because the REST paths are /users/* and the GraphQL root is User - authApi's commented-out resetPassword targets a different /auth/reset-password endpoint and is left untouched
- userQueries.ts: register ChangePassword and ResetPassword (root User, inputs ChangePasswordInput!/ResetPasswordInput!) at "/users/change_password/:id" PATCH and "/users/reset_password" POST - without these hybridBaseQuery returns a hard CUSTOM_ERROR, since the no-REST-fallback change in 0.28.8 means a missing GQL_MAP entry is a user-facing failure rather than a silent REST retry. "/users/reset_password" also matches the "/users/:id" pattern, but that entry defines no POST so matchUrl's definesMethod guard skips it, exactly as it already does for "/users/add"; "/users/change_password/:id" is three segments and collides with nothing (both verified by replaying matchUrl's regex against all 159 registered GQL_MAP keys)
- ResetPasswordModal.tsx: security fix - the raw fetch deliberately sent no Authorization header ("ใช้ API ใหม่ที่ไม่ต้องมี Authorization header"), making POST /users/reset_password an unauthenticated "set any user's password given email + username" primitive, with no permission check anywhere except the render-site gate in UserMetaCard. Now goes through useResetPasswordMutation so baseQueryFactory attaches the Bearer token and the BFF can enforce the permission server-side; adds an in-modal canResetOthers guard (user.reset_password or system admin) because the component is exported and independently importable. The client-side check is defence in depth only - the endpoint is not actually closed until the backend adds the server-side check
- ChangePasswordModal.tsx: migrate to useChangePasswordMutation, dropping the hand-built Bearer header read from localStorage("access_token") (which missed sessionStorage/rememberMe=false tokens) and the @/cms/utils/constants APP_CONFIG import from a core component; add a missing-userId guard
- both modals: replace the HTTP-status success test with an envelope check via the previously-unused src/core/utils/apiResponseStatus.ts (these are its first consumers). Under GraphQL every response is HTTP 200, so !response.ok never fired and a business failure - including a wrong current password - read as success; readEnvelopeStatus's "unknown" is deliberately treated as failure here, since a false failure costs a retry while a false success tells the user their password changed when it did not. The 400/401 branches are kept in catch for REST mode. Errors surface the BFF's own wording via readEnvelopeMessage(err.data) rather than readMutationError, whose String(error) fallback would render "[object Object]" in the error box
- UserProfileContext.tsx: rewritten as a thin RTK composition - deleted the local apiFetch helper, the fetchRef guard, the ~165-line fetchData and the three useEffect state mirrors, replaced by useGetUserRolesQuery + useGetUserByUserNameQuery (both already GraphQL-mapped) alongside the existing organizationApi queries, with useMemo-derived dropdowns and a memoized context value. Three bugs fall out of the rewrite: refetchUserData was permanently dead (fetchRef.current was set true on entry and reset only on failure paths, so every call after the first success returned early); getCurrentLanguage() was hardcoded to "en" while the app default is th, so role/department/command/station names never followed the language switcher and now read from useTranslation(); and loading tracked only the manual fetch, so UserOrganizationCard rendered N/A while the org dropdown queries were still in flight. Username now comes from useAuth().state.user - AuthProvider hydrates it synchronously from TokenManager on first render - instead of re-parsing localStorage["profile"]

Note: deliberately left out of scope - the 0-byte EditUserInfoCard.tsx, the try/catch-around-useUserProfile() pattern in UserMetaCard/UserInfoCard/UserOrganizationCard, the || JSX chains in UserMetaCard, and the UserFormProfile vs UserProfile type split
